text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 fired for service=private-vpc-control-plane (alert=control-plane-heartbeat-loss) :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-9342 created -> assigned to Sandeep (oncall)
Sandeep (oncall): acked via PD. I'm taking it. Any idea who's impacted?
AcmeOps (customer): we're seeing control plane timeouts from our side, flows to 10.2.3.4 drop intermittently.
Sandeep (oncall): confirmed hit on customer AcmeCorp (VPC-id vpc-0acme). Impact: control plane API calls time out, agents stop reporting.
Jamie R: ok — Sandeep, want me to take data-plane checks while you look at control plane?
Sandeep (oncall): yes please. Check agent heartbeats + route table for vpc-0acme. I'll pull control-plane logs and LB health.
Jamie R: running quick commands on infra host:
```
# check agent heartbeats
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=private-agent -o wide | grep vpc-0acme
# tcpdump on agent subnet (capture 60s)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.3.4 -w /tmp/acme.pcap
```
Jamie R: saw frequent RSTs from 10.2.3.4 -> control-plane on 443, spikes at 09:14-09:16 UTC. Possible intermediate NAT flaps.
Carol - eng-runtime: I'm tailing control-plane logs for that customer, seeing repeated failed heartbeat ack: "kv_sync: timeout waiting for agent ack (agent_id=acme-agent-7)"
Sandeep (oncall): thanks. Carol, can you check LB healthchecks and backend node metrics? Also dump the last 200 lines from control-plane service for that customer.
Carol - eng-runtime: pasted excerpts:
```
[2026-03-14T09:13:42Z] control-plane: heartbeat recv timeout agent=acme-agent-7 seq=129
[2026-03-14T09:13:55Z] control-plane: conn reset by peer peer_ip=10.2.3.4
[2026-03-14T09:14:10Z] control-plane: heartbeat recv timeout agent=acme-agent-8 seq=47
```
Carol - eng-runtime: LB health shows backend node i-0cpl01 flapping Unhealthy->Healthy every ~30s around the same window.
AcmeOps (customer): we didn't change anything. We do have a firewall vendor scheduled maintenance window earlier but they said it ended at 08:50.
Sandeep (oncall): hypothesis: intermediate network device (NAT/firewall) is resetting long-lived TLS connections causing agent heartbeats to drop. Impact: agents transiently disconnect -> control plane marks agents offline -> customer API calls fail.
Amber (handoff): I'm coming on shift in 15m. Sandeep, if you need to hand off after initial mitigation, ping me.
Sandeep (oncall): plan:
1) Confirm it's network (Jamie to get pcap + traceroute)
2) If network confirmed, recommend customer temporarily rotate to hosted control plane or enable agent reconnect backoff reduction (quick config)
3) Place a temporary routing policy to prefer region-b fallback for this customer's control-plane traffic to reduce impact while we work with their network team
4) Create incident ticket with timeline and customer comms draft
Jamie R: pcap shows repeated TCP FIN+ACK from intermediate 192.0.2.1 -> 10.2.3.4 at 09:14:52, 09:15:20, 09:15:48. Traceroute from control-plane to 10.2.3.4 shows hop 4 (192.0.2.1) latency spikes then packet loss.
Sandeep (oncall): tagging network-eng and accounts to engage customer: @carol-net (not in channel) and @accounts for contacting AcmeOps.
Deploy-bot: Suggested mitigation: rollback of recent control-plane kernel param change? No recent deploys to this service in last 24h.
Jamie R: I've asked AcmeOps to check their firewall logs for entries around 09:14 UTC. They replied: "we see NAT timeouts matching those timestamps, and the vendor confirms a transient control-plane of their edge box during rolling update."
AcmeOps (customer): vendor just confirmed they rolled a minor update that briefly doubled connection churn around 09:13-09:16. They recommended increasing idle TCP timeout or using shorter heartbeat intervals.
Carol - eng-runtime: we can push smaller heartbeat interval as a customer-side config toggle (no infra change) to make reconnects faster. Patch command snippet:
```
# apply transient agent config
redwoodctl private-agent update-config --customer vpc-0acme --heartbeat-interval 6s
```
Sandeep (oncall): Good. Carol, prepare a runbook step and patch. Jamie, assist customer with firewall timeout config and coordinate with accounts for comms.
Jamie R: sending AcmeOps the config snippet and monitoring guidance. Also will open a ticket with their vendor to request change to NAT idle timeout.
Amber (handoff): I'm ready to take over if this extends. Sandeep, send me the PD incident link and a short summary when you hand off.
Sandeep (oncall): handoff note:
- Problem: transient NAT/firewall rolling update at customer edge causing TLS resets -> agent heartbeats dropped -> control-plane marked agents offline -> API timeouts
- Mitigation done: patched heartbeat interval to 6s, advised customer vendor on NAT idle timeout, created routing fallback policy for reduced impact
- Next actions: monitor for 30m, confirm vendor permanent fix, update postmortem with timeline and recommendations
Sandeep (oncall): handing off to Amber in 10m. PD incident INC-9342 remains open.
Amber (handoff): acknowledged. I'll monitor and coordinate any escalations.
pagerduty-bot: INC-9342 status -> acknowledged by Sandeep (oncall).
incident-bot: automated post to #incidents-log will follow with timeline and links once incident is closed. :white_check_mark:
Jamie R: final note — after heartbeat interval change we saw reconnections within ~12s and control-plane error rate dropped to baseline.
AcmeOps (customer): thanks, we're stable now. We'll follow up with vendor for permanent NAT timeout increase.
Sandeep (oncall): closing loop — I'll file postmortem draft and include vendor evidence. Marking this as mitigated at 09:40 UTC.
